3D solar system Explorer is an interactive, browser-based 3D visualization web application built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js.

* Core Functionality: Users can explore a dynamic 3D model of the solar system by dragging to orbit, scrolling to zoom, and adjusting the orbital simulation speed (e.g., 1.0x).

* Interactive Inspection: Clicking on any planet, moon, or celestial body in 3D space—or selecting it via the navigation bar—opens an information panel displaying its classification (such as Terrestrial Planet), a brief description, and key planetary details.

* Architecture: Developed as a lightweight, single-file web app (index.html) designed for smooth, real-time 3D rendering directly in the browser without external backend dependencies.

[11:31 AM, 11/14/2026] Mazin Zabady: The 3D Solar System Explorer is an interactive, browser-based 3D visualization web application that simulates our solar system in real time. Users can freely navigate 3D space by dragging to orbit around celestial bodies, scrolling to zoom in and out, and dynamically adjusting the orbital simulation speed (e.g., 1.0x). Clicking on any planet, moon, or celestial body—or selecting it through the quick navigation bar—smoothly focuses the camera on that object and opens an educational side panel displaying its classification (such as Terrestrial Planet), core description, and planetary metrics.

Traditional 2D diagrams and textbooks often make it difficult for students and enthusiasts to grasp orbital mechanics, relative planetary positions, and spatial relationships in space. This project transforms astronomy education into an intuitive, hands-on experience. By making space exploration accessible directly through any standard web browser without requiring heavy installations or specialized hardware, it aims to inspire curiosity, enhance spatial understanding, and support STEM learning for students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide.

To develop this project, our team used HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+), powered by the Three.js (WebGL) library for real-time 3D rendering, lighting, camera controls, and orbital animations, along with Google Fonts for clean UI typography. The entire application is built as a lightweight, self-contained single-file web app (index.html) hosted on OneApp for instant, zero-setup access across both desktop and mobile browsers without external backend dependencies.

What makes our project creative is the combination of scientific clarity with an engaging, game-like user interface. Key design factors our team considered include:

* Performance and Accessibility: Optimizing the codebase into a single lightweight file to ensure smooth frame rates and fast loading times on standard consumer devices.

* Intuitive User Experience (UX): Offering dual navigation so users can either explore freely in 3D space or jump directly between the 9 featured celestial bodies using a clean bottom navigation bar and live speed controller.

* Educational Clarity: Structuring the side information panel so complex astronomical details are presented in bite-sized, easy-to-read cards without cluttering the visual space.
